$comment: Machine-readable design/balance contract for Pulse Cube. Every number here is asserted by tests/logic.test.ts or scripts/smoke.mjs; changing one without changing the tests should fail the suite.
name: Pulse Cube

renderer.type: orthographic side view, uniform scale on both axes
renderer.$comment: The cap was 2.5 in 1.0.0 (the raw devicePixelRatio of the test phones). Capping to 2 cuts the 390x844 backing store from 975x2110 to 780x1688, ~36% fewer pixels per frame. Screen-space shake is unaffected: the shake*dpr term runs under setTransform(identity), so the *dpr is a CSS->device unit conversion, not an amplitude.

loop.$stepComment: 1/240. At 10.4 cubes/s a 50ms frame moves the cube half its own width, enough to clip a spike corner or skip a landing; slicing to ~4ms makes every contact a real overlap.
loop.prng: none - levels are hand-authored, there is no procedural generation

derivedJumpArc.$comment: Every level is laid out against these four numbers. Platform tops sit at 2 and 4; floor gaps stay at or under 3 cubes; only a pad is asked to clear more.

camera.$comment: The cube sits 30% across the screen so the next hazard is always on screen before it is actionable. Scale is uniform on both axes - a cube that is not square is not a cube - so a tall phone trades view width for sky, never for readable lead time.

rules: held-ness is a set of active sources keyed by pointerId / key code
every NEW source is a press, so a second finger landing while the first is still down still jumps (fixed in 1.1.0; the empty->non-empty gate swallowed it)
one touch is exactly one press - the set dedupes by pointerId - and a re-armed buffer cannot double-jump because the buffer only spends on a grounded or coyote frame
keyboard auto-repeat is not a new press (e.repeat is ignored)
release fires only when the last source goes; pointerup, pointercancel, window blur and visibilitychange all clear every source
pointerdown on a button does not jump
input.$comment: touch-action:none is scoped to the play surface only. <body> gets touch-action:manipulation + overscroll-behavior:none, so the overlay panel stays scrollable on a short screen while play never scrolls the page.

levels.name: First Light
levels.design: one obstacle at a time, always with a long clear run-up; nowhere needs two jumps back to back

hazards.box: drawn 1x1, TESTED inset by 0.28 in x and trimmed 0.2 off the top
hazards.silhouette: upward triangle, distinct from every solid
hazards.$comment: A pixel-perfect triangle is unfair at this speed - the player reads the tip, not the base - so the hitbox matches what the eye expects. The cube is inset 0.08 by the same argument.

hazards.box: absence of ground; death below y = -6
hazards.silhouette: a hole in the floor band

hazards.box: solid, tested against the exact cube with no inset
hazards.$comment: Insetting the cube box would leave a sliver of air it can never close in one slice at this gravity, so it would fall through its own floor.

normal.onDeath: restart the level from the start
normal.$comment: The only mode that feeds best-progress. Classic core loop, unchanged.

practice.onDeath: respawn at the last passed checkpoint
practice.$comment: Deliberately separated from classic scoring so practice can never inflate a recorded best.

progression.metric: best progress through the level, as a percentage
progression.instantRetry: one action on the game-over overlay, or the same button that jumps
progression.rewards: optional; no streaks, no ads, no payments, no gating of play

effects.bounded: exactly one burst per death, cleared on reset and filtered by life; there is no spawner that can grow unbounded
effects.beat: a pulse synchronised to the level bpm; brightness only, never a full-screen flash
effects.determinismInvariant: reduced mode changes DRAWING only. state.shake, state.particles and the beat value are all still simulated and still advance identically, so collision and scoring are bit-identical between the two modes.
effects.persistence: an explicit choice is stored and wins over the media query; with no stored choice the media query decides

audio.$hideComment: visibilitychange pauses a run in progress (game.ts); the same event also clears every held input source (input.ts).

onboarding.type: text on the start overlay over a live scene, dismissed by starting
teaches: the cube runs on its own
hold to jump again the moment you land
the bar at the top is progress

assets.$comment: Everything is drawn with Canvas 2D primitives and all sound is synthesised with WebAudio oscillators. Fonts are the system-ui stack. No third-party asset is bundled.
